hints.title: Interpret each number as a horizontal-line intersection count
hints.body: The numbers p, q, r and s count intersections of the same graph with the levels y=1, 2, 3 and 4. Every offered list contains a count of four.
hints.recap: Four distinct intersections force a genuine quartic with three turning points.
hints.pitfall: Do not draw four unrelated sketches for the four levels.
hints.pause: Sketch the W-shaped and upside-down W-shaped possibilities.

recall.reminder: Use turning heights and monotonic sections to count roots at a specified level.

hints.title: Mark the three turning heights
hints.body: For a W-shaped graph, mark the two minimum heights and the intervening maximum, then count crossings below, at and above each.
hints.recap: Tangency counts as one distinct solution.
hints.pitfall: All four levels belong to one graph.
hints.pause: Build the possible changes in count as the horizontal level rises.

recall.reminder: Tangency counts as one distinct solution.

hints.title: Test each proposed sequence
hints.body: An odd number of crossings forces a turning point on that level; carry that turning height into the checks at the other levels.
hints.recap: Turning heights constrain several counts at once.
hints.pitfall: Moving a turn to repair one count may spoil another.
hints.pause: Find which proposed sequence cannot be realised by one quartic.

recall.reminder: Assume the proposed counts all hold for one graph, then check whether those assumptions force incompatible intersection counts.

solution:
Consider B, which proposes counts 1, 3, 2, 4. Four intersections at height 4 require three turning points. The single intersection at height 1 forces the upward W shape with its lower minimum at height 1; a downward shape with a single intersection at height 1 would have no intersections above that highest point.

The count of three at height 2 forces the second minimum to have height 2. The central maximum must exceed 4. Consequently the line y=3 cuts the graph four times, contradicting the proposed count of two. B is impossible.
knowledgePattern: Constrain horizontal-line intersection counts of a quartic
